Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 1:

﴿O you who have believed, fulfill (all) contracts﴾ meaning: the binding covenants that you have made with Allah and with the people. Then he began another statement and said: ﴿Lawful for you are the animals of grazing livestock﴾. It was said: they are the livestock themselves, namely camels, cattle and sheep. And it was said: "the animals of grazing livestock" refers to their wild counterparts, such as gazelles, wild oxen and wild asses. ﴿except what is recited to you﴾ (i.e., what is read to you in the Qur'an), meaning His saying: ﴿Prohibited to you are carrion﴾ and the rest of the verse, ﴿excluding game while you are in the state of ihram﴾, meaning: unless you hunt game while in the state of ihram, for it is not lawful for you to do so. ﴿Indeed, Allah ordains what He wills﴾: He makes lawful whatever He wills and prohibits whatever He wills.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 2:

﴿O you who have believed, do not violate the rites of Allah﴾, meaning: the offerings marked for slaughter at Makkah. This verse was revealed concerning al-Hutam ibn Dubay'ah, who raided the herd of Madinah and took it off to al-Yamamah. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set out in the year of al-Qada' (the year of the making up of the pilgrimage), he heard the talbiyah of the pilgrims of al-Yamamah, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This is al-Hutam; go after him!" He had garlanded what he had plundered from the herd of Madinah and offered it to the Ka'bah. When they set out in pursuit of him, Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿do not violate the rites of Allah﴾, meaning: what has been marked for Allah, that is, made known [as an offering]; ﴿nor the sacred month﴾ by fighting in it; ﴿nor the offering﴾, which is everything offered to the House of Allah: a camel, a cow, or a sheep; ﴿nor the garlands﴾, meaning: the offerings garlanded with bark from the trees of the Sacred Precinct; ﴿nor those coming to the Sacred House﴾, those intending it from among the polytheists.

The exegetes said: In the pre-Islamic era, wars were ongoing among the Arabs except in the sacred months. Whoever was found outside them was attacked, unless he was one who had marked his animal, or was driving offerings, or had garlanded himself or his camel with bark from the trees of the Sacred Precinct, or was in a state of ihram; these were not to be harmed. Allah the Glorious and Exalted therefore commanded the Muslims to maintain this security as it had been, for a kind of benefit, until He abrogated it with His saying: ﴿So kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾, and His saying: ﴿seeking bounty from their Lord﴾, meaning: profit through trade, ﴿and approval﴾, through the pilgrimage in their supposition. ﴿And when you have come out of ihram﴾, ﴿then hunt﴾: a command of permission. ﴿And do not let the hatred of a people﴾, ﴿hatred of a people﴾, meaning: the people of Makkah, ﴿because they had barred you from al-Masjid al-Haram﴾, meaning: in the year of al-Hudaybiyah, ﴿not to transgress﴾ against the pilgrims of al-Yamamah by permitting for yourselves what is forbidden from them. ﴿And cooperate﴾, so let one of you help another, ﴿in righteousness﴾, which is what I have commanded, ﴿and piety﴾, abandoning what I have forbidden. ﴿And do not cooperate in sin﴾, meaning: disobedience to Allah, ﴿and aggression﴾, transgressing its limits. Then He warned them, saying: ﴿And fear Allah﴾, so do not make lawful what is forbidden. ﴿Indeed, Allah is severe in penalty﴾ when He punishes.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 3:

﴿Forbidden to you is carrion﴾. The explanation of this verse was given in Surat al-Baqarah up to His words: ﴿and that which has been strangled﴾, meaning the one that is choked and dies, for whatever reason it may be; ﴿and that which has been beaten to death﴾, meaning the one killed by being struck; ﴿and that which has fallen from a height﴾, meaning the one that falls from above to below and dies; ﴿and that which has been gored﴾, meaning the one killed by goring; ﴿and that which has been eaten of by a beast of prey﴾, meaning what remains of it after the beast has eaten from it is forbidden. Then He made an exception of whatever can be slaughtered (lit. whose dhakat is attainable) from all of these prohibited things, and said: ﴿except what you have slaughtered﴾, i.e., except what you have slaughtered; ﴿and what is sacrificed on the stone altars﴾, i.e., what is sacrificed in the name of idols, is forbidden; ﴿and that you seek decision by divining arrows﴾, i.e., seek to learn, by means of the arrows, what has been apportioned to you of good and evil. The arrows (al-azlam) are the shafts that the people of the Jahiliyyah used to shuffle when they wanted to decide a matter. ﴿That﴾, i.e., seeking decision through the arrows, ﴿is grave disobedience﴾, a departure from the lawful to the unlawful. ﴿Today﴾, meaning: the Day of Arafah in the year the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) performed Hajj after the Conquest. ﴿The disbelievers have despaired﴾ of your returning to their religion. ﴿So do not fear them﴾ regarding supporting Muhammad and following his religion, ﴿but fear Me﴾ regarding the worship of idols. ﴿Today﴾, meaning: the Day of Arafah, ﴿I have perfected for you your religion﴾, i.e., the rulings of your religion, so that after this verse no further lawful or unlawful matter was revealed. ﴿And I have completed My favor upon you﴾, meaning: by entering Makkah in safety as I promised you. ﴿But whoever is forced﴾ to eat what has been forbidden of the things mentioned in this verse ﴿by severe hunger﴾, i.e., by famine, ﴿without intending sin﴾, i.e., without deliberately committing disobedience, which is that he eats beyond what satisfies him, or that he is disobedient by his journey, ﴿then indeed, Allah is Forgiving﴾ to him for what he ate of what was forbidden to him, ﴿Merciful﴾ toward His friends, in that He has granted them this concession.

**Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 4:**

﴿They ask you what has been made lawful for them.﴾ ʿAdiyy ibn Ḥātim asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), saying: "We hunt with dogs and hawks (*buzah*), and Allah has forbidden carrion (*al-maytah*). So what is lawful for us from it?" Then this verse was revealed: ﴿Say: The good things have been made lawful for you.﴾ That is, what the Arabs find good (*yastaṭībuhu*). This is the basis of permissibility (*al-taḥlīl*). So every animal that the Arabs find good, such as the dabb (spiny-tailed lizard), the jerboa, and the hare, is lawful, and whatever the Arabs find repugnant is unlawful. ﴿And what you have trained﴾ means: and the game caught by what you have trained, ﴿of the hunting animals (*al-jawāriḥ*)﴾, which are the predators that catch prey, including birds of prey, dogs, and beasts of prey, ﴿trained (*mukallibīn*)﴾, meaning teaching them to hunt, ﴿you teach them from what Allah has taught you﴾, meaning you train them to pursue game. ﴿Then eat of what they catch for you﴾: this applies to these hunting animals even if they kill, provided they did not eat from it. If they did eat from it, then the apparent ruling is that it is unlawful. ﴿And mention the name of Allah over it﴾ at the time of releasing the hunting animals.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 5:

﴿Today the good things have been made lawful for you﴾ which you asked about. ﴿And the food of those who were given the Book is lawful for you, and your food is lawful for them﴾, meaning: it is lawful for you to feed them. ﴿And chaste women﴾, the modest ones, ﴿from among the believing women, and chaste women﴾, the free ones, ﴿from among those who were given the Book﴾, from the People of the Book, ﴿when you have given them their wages﴾, meaning: their dowries, ﴿being chaste﴾, married, ﴿not fornicators﴾, openly committing adultery, ﴿nor those who take secret lovers﴾, secretly committing adultery with them. ﴿And whoever disbelieves in faith﴾, in God, in whom belief is obligatory, ﴿his deeds are nullified﴾ if he dies in that state, ﴿and he, in the Hereafter, will be among the losers﴾, those who have lost the reward.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 6:

﴿O you who have believed, when you intend to stand for prayer﴾, i.e., when you wish to rise to it, ﴿wash your faces and your hands to the elbows﴾, meaning: along with the elbows, ﴿and wipe over your heads and wash your feet to the ankles﴾, and they are the two protrusions on either side of the foot. ﴿And if you are in a state of janabah, then purify yourselves﴾, i.e., bathe. ﴿And if you are ill﴾ is explained in Surat al-Nisa’ up to His saying: ﴿Allah does not intend to make difficulty for you﴾, meaning, hardship in the religion, but He has made it easy by the concession of tayammum. ﴿But He intends to purify you﴾ from minor and major impurities and sins, because wudu' expiates sins. ﴿And to complete His favor upon you﴾ by clarifying the legislated rulings, ﴿and that you may be grateful﴾ for My favor, so that you obey My command.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 7:

﴿And remember the favour of Allah upon you﴾ — by Islam — ﴿and His covenant with which He bound you﴾. That is: when you pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to hear and obey in everything he commanded and forbade. This is His saying: ﴿when you said﴾ when you said ﴿"We hear and we obey." And fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾ — the hidden things of the hearts.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 8:

﴿O you who have believed, be persistent in standing firm for Allah, witnesses in justice﴾ you stand for Allah in every truth that obligates you to uphold it. ﴿And do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just﴾ do not let the enmity of a people carry you to abandon justice. ﴿Be just﴾ toward the friend and the enemy alike. ﴿That is nearer to righteousness﴾ i.e., justice is closer to guarding oneself against the Fire.

O you who have believed, remember the favor of Allah upon you (Qur'an 5:11). This means: the favor Allah bestowed upon His Prophet when he came to the Jews, he and a group of his companions, seeking their help regarding a blood-money (diya), and they conspired among themselves to drop a millstone (rahā) upon them. Allah informed him of this through (the tongue of) Jibril, so they departed. Then He related the breaking of the covenant of Allah by the Children of Israel, just as this group broke the covenant that was between them and the Messenger of Allah when they intended to assassinate him with it, so He said:

And God had certainly taken the covenant of the Children of Israel, on the condition that they would act upon what is in the Torah (al-Tawrah). ﴿And We raised up﴾, meaning We established by that, ﴿from among them twelve chiefs﴾ (nuqaba', sing. naqib), meaning guarantors and sureties, who guaranteed on behalf of their people their fulfilment of the covenant. ﴿And God said﴾ to them: ﴿Indeed, I am with you﴾, with help and support: ﴿If you establish prayer and give zakah (obligatory alms) and believe in My messengers and support them﴾, meaning: honour them; ﴿and lend God a goodly loan﴾, meaning: charity to the poor and the needy. ﴿Whoever disbelieves after that﴾, meaning: after this covenant and pledge, ﴿then he has certainly strayed from the even path﴾, meaning: he has missed the intended course of the way.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 13:

﴿So for their breaking their covenant﴾ — i.e., by their breaking it — ﴿We cursed them﴾ — i.e., We removed them from Our mercy — ﴿and made their hearts hard﴾ — dry, barren of faith. ﴿They distort words﴾ — they change the speech of God ﴿from their places﴾ — concerning the description of Muhammad (ﷺ) in their scripture and the verse of stoning. ﴿And they have forgotten a portion of what they were reminded of﴾ — they abandoned a share of what they were commanded in their scripture, namely following Muhammad. ﴿And you will not cease to discover treachery﴾ — O Muhammad — ﴿among them﴾ — treachery such as they showed you when they intended to kill you. ﴿Except a few of them﴾ — meaning: those who embraced Islam. ﴿So pardon them and overlook﴾ — abrogated by the verse of the sword. ﴿Indeed, Allah loves the doers of good﴾ — those who overlook.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 14:

﴿And from those who say, "We are Christians," We took their covenant,﴾ just as We took the covenant of the Jews, ﴿but they forgot a portion of what they were reminded of﴾ so they abandoned what they had been commanded, namely belief in Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿So We incited among them enmity and hatred﴾ that is, We cast enmity and hatred between the Jews and the Christians ﴿until the Day of Resurrection. And Allah will inform them of what they used to do﴾ a warning to them. Then He called them to belief in Muhammad, peace be upon him, saying:

O People of the Scripture, there has come to you Our Messenger, [Muhammad], making clear to you much of what you used to conceal of the Scripture and overlooking much. There has come to you from Allah a light and a clear Book.

(Al-Wahidi, al-Wajiz, on Surah al-Ma'idah 5:15)

﴿يا أهل الكتاب﴾ means: the Jews and the Christians. ﴿قد جاءكم رسولنا﴾ means: Muhammad. ﴿يُبَيِّنُ لَكُمْ كَثِيرًا مِمَّا كُنْتُمْ تُخْفُونَ مِنَ الكتاب﴾ means: you conceal what is in the Torah and the Gospel, such as the verse of stoning and the description of Muhammad, peace be upon him. ﴿ويعفو عن كثير﴾ means: he overlooks much, so he does not inform you of your concealing it. ﴿قد جاءكم من الله نور﴾ means: the Prophet. ﴿وكتاب مبين﴾ means: the Qur'an, in which there is clarification of everything about which you differ.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 16:

﴿Through it Allah guides﴾ meaning: through the Clear Book. ﴿Whoever follows His pleasure﴾ follows what Allah is pleased with, namely affirming Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿The ways of peace﴾ the paths of safety, whoever takes them is safe in his religion. ﴿And brings them out of darknesses﴾ disbelief ﴿into light﴾ faith ﴿by His permission﴾ by His enabling and His will. ﴿And guides them to a straight path﴾ which is Islam.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 17:

﴿Indeed, they have disbelieved who say, "Indeed, Allah is the Messiah, the son of Mary."﴾ He means: those who took him as a god (ilah). ﴿Say, "Then who could prevent anything from Allah if He wished to destroy the Messiah"﴾ That is: who could ward off anything of the punishment of Allah? ﴿If He wished to destroy the Messiah﴾ That is: to punish him. Had he been a god, he would have been able to ward off that.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 18:

﴿And the Jews and the Christians said: "We are the children of Allah and His beloved."﴾ As for the Jews, they said: Allah, out of His tenderness and compassion toward us, is like a compassionate father. As for the Christians, they interpreted the words of ʿIsā: "When you pray, say: 'Our Father who art in heaven, hallowed be His name'" (Our Father, who art in heaven), and he meant that He is in His goodness and mercy toward His righteous servants, like a merciful father. It was also said: they meant "We are the children of the messengers of Allah." They only said this when the Prophet ﷺ warned them of Allah's punishment, so Allah said: ﴿Say: "Why then does He punish you for your sins?"﴾ That is: why then did He punish those before you for their sins, such as the people of the Sabbath and others. ﴿Nay, you are but human beings of those whom He has created﴾, like the rest of the children of Adam. ﴿He forgives whom He wills﴾, those who repent from Judaism, ﴿and punishes whom He wills﴾, those who die upon it.
And His saying: ﴿After a lull in the messengers﴾ means after a break in the prophets. ﴿Lest you should say﴾ means lest you say: ﴿There came to us no bringer of good tidings and no warner﴾.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 20:

And His saying: ﴿And made you kings﴾, meaning: He made for you servants and retinue, and they were the first of the children of Adam to possess servants and retinue. ﴿And gave you what He had not given anyone else in the worlds﴾: from the splitting of the sea for you and the drowning of your enemy, and the manna and the quails, and other things besides that.

O my people, enter the Holy Land (al-ard al-muqaddasah), the purified land, meaning: al-Sham (Syria). It is so called because it was purified from polytheism and made a dwelling for the prophets. ﴿Which Allah has written for you﴾, that is, Allah has commanded you to enter it. ﴿And do not turn back on your heels﴾, that is, do not return to your polytheistic religion, associating partners with Allah.
They said, "O Musa, indeed in it there are a people of tyrants" — tall, possessing strength; and they were from the remnants of 'Ad, who are called the Amalaqah (the Amalekites).

"Two men said" — they were Yusha' ibn Nun and Kaleb ibn Yufunna — "among those who feared" God in opposing His command, "upon whom God had bestowed favour": with grace and certainty. ﴿Enter upon them through the gate﴾, and the verse continues. They said this out of certainty in God's victory and in the fulfilment of His promise to His Prophet. The others, however, opposed their prophet, disobeyed God's command, and uttered words by which they transgressed; and that is His saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 24:

﴿They said, "O Musa, we will never enter it as long as they remain within it. So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting right here."﴾ Then Musa said at that time:

﴿I have no power except over myself and my brother﴾ means: none of them obeyed me except myself and my brother. ﴿So part us from the defiant people﴾ means: judge between us and the disobedient people. So God forbade those who disobeyed to enter the town, and confined them in the wilderness (al-tih) for forty years, until they died. None of these entered it; rather, their children entered it. This is His saying:

Verse 26 of Surah al-Ma'idah, as quoted by al-Wahidi in al-Wajiz:

﴿Indeed, it is forbidden to them﴾ and so on. And His saying: ﴿they will wander bewildered in the land﴾ meaning, they will be perplexed and will not be guided to find a way out of it. ﴿So do not grieve over the defiantly disobedient people﴾ meaning, do not grieve over their punishment.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 27:

﴿And recite to them﴾ meaning: to your people, ﴿the news﴾ the account ﴿of the two sons of Adam﴾, Habil (Abel) and Qabil (Cain), ﴿when they both offered a sacrifice﴾. Habil drew near to God with the best ram of his flock, and fire descended from the sky and consumed it; it is the ram with which Isma'il was ransomed. Qabil drew near to God with the worst of the wheat he had, for he was a man of crops, and the fire did not consume his offering. The qurban (sacrifice, offering) is the name for everything by which one draws near to God. Then the one whose offering was not accepted said: ﴿I will surely kill you﴾, out of envy towards him. Habil said: ﴿Indeed, God accepts only from the righteous﴾ who guard against sins (not from the sinners).

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 28:

﴿If you stretch your hand toward me to kill me﴾ — if you begin to kill me, I will not be the one who begins to kill you; ﴿indeed I fear Allah﴾ — in killing you.
﴿Indeed, I want you to bear my sin and your sin﴾: that you bear the sin of my killing and the sin of what you had committed before killing me.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 30:

﴿Then his soul made it easy for him to kill his brother﴾: it made it smooth for him and adorned that for him. ﴿So he killed him, and became among the losers﴾: he lost his worldly life by angering his parents, and his Hereafter by the wrath of God upon him. When he killed him, he did not know what to do with him, because he was the first dead person on the face of the earth from among the children of Adam, so he carried him in a sack on his back.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 31:

﴿Then Allah sent a crow scratching in the earth﴾, stirring up dust from the earth over a dead crow, ﴿to show him how to conceal﴾, to cover up, ﴿the dead body﴾, the corpse, ﴿of his brother﴾. When he saw that, he said: ﴿"Woe to me! Am I unable to be like this crow and conceal the dead body of my brother?" And he became among the regretful﴾, over carrying it and wandering around with it.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 32:

﴿Because of that﴾ — from the cause of that which Qabil (Cain) did. ﴿We prescribed﴾ — We obligated ﴿upon the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul, without (it being in retaliation for) a soul,﴾ — without qawad (legal retaliation) ﴿or corruption﴾ — shirk (associating partners with God) ﴿in the earth, it is as if he had killed all of mankind.﴾ — He is to be killed as if he had killed them all, and he will burn in the Fire as he would burn had he killed them all. ﴿And whoever gives it life﴾ — prohibits it and abstains from killing it ﴿it is as if he had given life to all of mankind﴾ — by their safety from him, since he does not consider their blood lawful. ﴿And certainly Our messengers came to them﴾ — meaning the Children of Israel ﴿with clear proofs﴾ — that the truth of what they brought them is certain. ﴿Then indeed many of them, after that, in the earth, are transgressors﴾ — i.e., going beyond the bounds of the truth.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 33:

﴿Indeed, the penalty for those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger﴾ means: those who disobey them and do not obey them, i.e., those who rise up against the Imam and against the community (ummah) with the sword. This verse was revealed concerning the story of the 'Uraniyyin, which is well known, as an instruction to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) regarding the punishment of whoever does the like of their deed. As for His saying: ﴿and strive upon the earth [to cause] corruption﴾, by killing and seizing property, ﴿[the penalty is] that they be killed, or crucified, or have their hands and feet cut off on opposite sides, or be exiled from the land.﴾ The meaning of "or" (aw) here is permission (al-ibahah), so the Imam may do whichever of these things he wishes. The meaning of exile from the land is imprisonment, because imprisonment is equivalent to being removed from the land (al-nafy min al-ard al-habs fi al-sijn li-anna al-majun bi-manzilat al-mukhraj min al-dunya). ﴿That is a disgrace for them﴾, meaning humiliation and public exposure, ﴿in this world, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment.﴾ This applies to the disbelievers concerning whom the verse was revealed, since the 'Uraniyyin apostatized from the religion. And when a Muslim is punished in this world for his crime, it becomes an expiation for him.

Qur'anic quotations: ﴿Except those who repent before you gain power over them﴾.

Commentary: "They believe before you punish them, and then God is Forgiving and Merciful toward them." This applies to the polytheist who wages war (al-muharib al-mushrik): if he believes before he is captured, all the prescribed penalties (hudud) are waived for him. As for the Muslim who wages war, if he repents and seeks safe-conduct (yasta'min) before he is captured, the penalties of God (hudud Allah) are waived for him, but the rights of the human beings (huquq Bani Adam) are not waived.

O you who have believed, fear Allah (i.e., the punishment of Allah) by obedience, and seek the means (al-wasilah) to Him, draw near to Him by obeying Him, and strive (jahadu) against the enemy in His way, in His obedience, so that you may succeed, that you may be happy and remain in Paradise.
﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve﴾ — the verse is clear.
﴿They wish﴾ they long for in their hearts ﴿to come out of the Fire﴾

The Qur'anic verse (keep markers):

﴿And as for the thief, male and female, cut off their hands﴾ — the right hand of this one and the right hand of that one, so the plural is used. ﴿As a recompense for what they committed, and as an exemplary punishment from Allah. And Allah is Mighty in His retribution, Wise in what He has made obligatory of amputation.﴾

Note on the translation of the gloss: "al-Wajiz" (the Concise) is the title of al-Wahidi's abridged commentary on the Qur'an.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 39:

﴿Whoever repents after his wrongdoing﴾ [i.e., toward] the people, ﴿and makes amends﴾ [i.e., his deeds] after the theft, ﴿then indeed Allah will turn to him [in forgiveness]﴾, [meaning] He returns to him with mercy.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 40:

﴿Do you not know that to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth? He punishes whom He wills﴾ for the minor sin, ﴿and forgives whom He wills﴾ for the major sin.

O Messenger, let not those grieve you who race to disbelief (إذ كنت موعودَ النَّصر عليهم), and they are the hypocrites, and this became clear to them by His saying: ﴿Among those who say, "We believe," with their mouths, but their hearts have not believed; and among the Jews are listeners to falsehood⦆, that is: a group who listen much to falsehood, ﴿listening to falsehood﴾, they hear from you in order to lie about you, so they say: "We heard from him such-and-such," when they did not hear it. ﴿Listeners for another people who have not come to you﴾, that is: they are spies for those absent folk, conveying your news to them. ﴿They distort words from after their places﴾, from after God had placed them in their places, meaning: the verse of stoning. ﴿They say: If you are given this, take it⦆, meaning: the Jews of Khaybar, with the lashing; and they are the ones mentioned in His saying: ﴿for another people who have not come to you﴾. This is because they sent to Qurayzah to ask Muhammad (ﷺ) for a ruling concerning the two married adulterers, and they said to them: "If he rules for lashing, accept it, and if he rules for stoning, do not accept it." That is His saying: ﴿If you are given this⦆, meaning: the lashing, ﴿take it⦆, accept it, ﴿and if you are not given it, beware⦆, lest you act upon it. ﴿And whoever God desires to test⦆, to misguide and to disbelief, ﴿you cannot avail him anything against God⦆, you cannot ward off God's punishment from him. ﴿Those are the ones⦆, that is: whoever God desires to test, they are those ﴿for whom God did not desire to purify their hearts⦆, to make their intentions sincere. ﴿For them in this world is disgrace⦆, by the exposing of their veils, ﴿and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment⦆, which is the Fire.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 42:

﴿Listeners to falsehood, devourers of what is unlawfully gained (al-suht)﴾, which is bribery in judgment. That is: the Jewish judges listen to falsehood from whoever comes to them in the wrong, and they take bribes from him and consume them. ﴿So if they come to you, either judge between them or turn away from them.﴾ Allah gave His Prophet the choice to judge between the People of the Book when they bring their dispute to him, then this was abrogated (naskh) by His saying: ﴿And judge between them by what Allah has revealed﴾ — the verse.

God expressed His wonder at His Prophet, peace be upon him, concerning the Jews' submission to his judgment (tahkīm, submitting a dispute to an arbiter), even though they knew what the Torah (al-Tawrah) contains regarding the judgment on the adulterer and its prescribed punishment. As for His saying, ﴿In it is the judgment of God﴾, it means: the stoning. ﴿Then they turn away after that﴾, after the arbitration, so they do not accept your judgment of stoning. ﴿And those are not believers﴾, those who turn away from the stoning.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 44:

﴿Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which is guidance﴾ — (it is) an explanation of the ruling about which they came to you seeking a decision. ﴿And light﴾ — an explanation that your affair is true. ﴿By it the prophets who submitted judged﴾ — from (the time of) Musa until ʿIsa. ﴿Who submitted﴾ — that is, they yielded to the ruling of the Torah. ﴿To those who became Jews﴾ — they repented of disbelief; and they are the Children of Israel until the time of ʿIsa. ﴿And the rabbis﴾ — the scholars (ʿulama'). ﴿And the rabbis (aḥbār)﴾ — the jurists (fuqaha'). ﴿By what they were entrusted with safekeeping﴾ — (istaḥfaẓū) were made responsible, that is, they were charged with preserving it from the Book of Allah; and it is said: (it means) acting upon what is in it, and that is its preservation. ﴿Of the Book of Allah, and they were witnesses to it﴾ — that it is from Allah. Then He addressed the Jews, saying: ﴿So do not fear the people﴾ — in making known the description of Muhammad (ﷺ) and the stoning. ﴿But fear Me﴾ — in concealing that. ﴿And do not exchange My signs﴾ — My rulings and My obligations ﴿for a small price﴾ — meaning: the goods of this world. ﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, those are the disbelievers﴾ — it was revealed concerning those among the Jews who altered the ruling of Allah, and it does not apply to the people of Islam; and there is nothing of it in the two verses that follow.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 45:

﴿And We prescribed for them therein﴾ We enjoined upon them in the Torah ﴿that the life [is to be taken] for life, the eye for eye﴾ (the verse continues). Whenever retaliation (qisas) applies between two persons in the matter of life, retaliation applies between them in all the limbs and extremities, provided they are equal in soundness. His saying ﴿and wounds are subject to retaliation﴾ applies to everything in which retaliation can be carried out, such as the two lips, the penis, the two testicles, the two buttocks, the two feet and the two hands. This is a generalization after the specification in His saying ﴿the eye for eye and the nose for nose﴾. ﴿But whoever forgoes it, it is an expiation for him﴾: whoever pardons and waives retaliation, it is forgiveness for him with Allah and a great reward.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 46:

﴿And We sent after them, following in their footsteps, Jesus son of Mary﴾ Meaning: We caused him to follow in the footsteps of the prophets, that is, We sent him after them, following on their traces. ﴿confirming what was before him of the Torah﴾ He affirms its rulings and calls to them. ﴿And We gave him the Gospel, in which was guidance and light, and confirming what was before it of the Torah, and a guidance and an admonition﴾ Its meaning: and a guide and an admonisher.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 47:

﴿And let the people of the Gospel judge by what Allah has revealed therein.﴾ That is: and We said to them, "Let them judge by this Book at that time."

**Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 48:**

﴿And We have sent down to you the Book in truth, confirming what came before it of the Book and as a guardian over it.﴾ That is: a witness, a trustee, a protector, and a watcher over the earlier books. So whatever the People of the Book tell you, if it is in the Qur'an, then believe it, and if not, then deny it. ﴿So judge between them﴾ between the Jews ﴿by what Allah has revealed﴾ in the Qur'an and the stoning (al-rajm). ﴿And do not follow their desires away from the truth that has come to you﴾ he says: do not follow them, abandoning the truth you have, and following them instead. ﴿For each of you We have made a law (shir'ah) and a way (minhaj)﴾ for the community of Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad (ﷺ), may blessings be upon them all: a path (sabil) and a custom (sunnah). So the Torah has its law, the Gospel has its law, and the Qur'an has its law. ﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have made you one community﴾ upon one matter, the religion of Islam. ﴿But to test you﴾ to examine you ﴿in what He has given you﴾ of the Book and the sunan. ﴿So race to good deeds﴾ hasten to righteous (al-zakiyah) actions ﴿To Allah is your return, all of you﴾ you and the People of the Book, ﴿and He will inform you about what you used to dispute﴾ concerning religion, obligations, and sunan. That is: the matter will end in that which removes doubts, through the certainty that will be attained.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 49:

﴿And beware of them lest they tempt you away from some of what Allah has revealed to you.﴾ That is: lest they lead you astray from the truth toward their own desires. It was revealed when the leaders of the Jews said to one another: "Come, let us go to Muhammad, perhaps we can tempt him and turn him back from what he is upon." So they came to him and said: "You know that if we follow you, the people will follow you. But we have a dispute, so judge for us against our opponents when we bring our case before you, and we will believe in you." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) refused that, and Allah revealed this verse: ﴿But if they turn away, then know that Allah only intends to afflict them for some of their sins.﴾ (That is: if they turn away from faith and from judging by the Qur'an, then know that this is because Allah wills to hasten their punishment in this world for some of their sins), and He will repay them in the Hereafter for all of them. Then their punishment in this world was exile and banishment. ﴿And indeed, many of the people are defiantly disobedient.﴾ He means: the Jews.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 50:

﴿Do they then seek the judgment of the Time of Ignorance (al-Jahiliyyah)?﴾ That is: do the Jews seek, concerning the adulterers, a judgment that God did not command, though they are People of the Book, as the people of the Jahiliyyah did? ﴿And who is better than God in judgment for a people who are certain?﴾ That is: whoever has certainty will see clearly the justice of God in His judgment. Then He forbade the believers from allying with the Jews and threatened them for it with His saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 52:

﴿So you see those in whose hearts is a disease⁠ ⁠﴾ meaning: ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy and his companions, ﴿hastening toward them⁠ ⁠﴾ into friendship with the People of the Book and aiding them against the Muslims by passing their news to them, ﴿saying, "We fear that a reversal of fortune may befall us⁠ ⁠﴾ meaning: that the affair may turn from its present state, they meaning: a drought, so that provisions and loans would be cut off from us," ﴿So perhaps Allah will bring a conquest⁠ ⁠﴾ meaning: for Muhammad over all who opposed him, ﴿or a command from Him⁠ ⁠﴾ to kill the hypocrites and expose their concealment, ﴿so they will become, over what they had concealed within themselves⁠ ⁠﴾ meaning: the people of hypocrisy, over what they had harbored of allegiance to the Jews and of passing news to them, ﴿regretful⁠ ⁠﴾.

﴿And those who believe will say﴾ the believers, when God exposes the hypocrites' concealment: ﴿Are these the ones﴾ meaning the hypocrites ﴿who swore by God, their most emphatic oaths﴾ they swore by the most binding oaths ﴿that they are truly with you﴾ that they are believers and your helpers against those who oppose you ﴿their deeds have become worthless﴾ every good they did was nullified by their disbelief ﴿and they have become losers﴾ they went to the Fire, and the believers inherited their dwellings in Paradise.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 54:

﴿O you who have believed, whoever among you reverts from his religion﴾ God, exalted is He, knew that a people would turn back from Islam after the death of their Prophet (ﷺ), so God, exalted is He, informed them that He would ﴿bring forth a people He loves and who love Him﴾ — and they are Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) and his companions who fought the people of apostasy (ridda) — ﴿humble toward the believers﴾, like a child to his father and a slave to his master, ﴿mighty against the disbelievers﴾, harsh toward them like a predator toward its prey. ﴿They strive in the way of Allah and do not fear the blame of any blamer﴾, unlike the hypocrites who used to watch the disbelievers and feared their blame in supporting the religion. ﴿That is the bounty of Allah﴾, meaning: their love for Allah, mighty and majestic is He, their gentleness toward the Muslims, and their severity toward the disbelievers are by a bounty from Allah upon them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 55:

﴿Your only walī (protector and ally) is Allah, and His Messenger, and those who believe, who establish prayer and give zakah while they bow in worship.﴾ It was revealed when the Jews shunned those among them who had embraced Islam. ʿAbdullah ibn Salam said: "O Messenger of Allah, our people have shunned us and sworn that they will not sit with us." So this verse was revealed, and he said: "We are content with Allah, His Messenger, and the believers as allies." As for His words ﴿while they bow﴾, it means: voluntary prayer (ṣalāh al-taṭawwuʿ).

﴿Whoever takes as allies Allah and His Messenger﴾ means whoever undertakes to carry out His obedience and to support His Messenger and the believers. ﴿Then indeed the party of Allah﴾, the army of Allah and the helpers of His religion, ﴿they are the victorious﴾. They overcame the Jews, so they expelled them from their homes. Abdullah ibn Salam and his companions remained, those who took Allah and His Messenger as allies.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 57:

﴿O you who have believed, do not take﴾ ... The verse was revealed concerning men who used to show friendship toward the hypocritical Jews. The meaning of His words ﴿those who have taken your religion as a mockery and amusement﴾ is their showing that with the tongue while concealing disbelief within themselves, as play and mockery. ﴿And the disbelievers﴾ means the polytheists of the Arabs and the disbelievers of Makkah. ﴿And fear Allah﴾, so do not take them as allies ﴿if you are believers﴾ in His promise and His warning.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 58:

﴿And when you call to prayer﴾ — you call people with the adhan (the call to prayer) — ﴿they take it as a mockery and a game﴾ — they laugh among themselves and wink at one another in a manner of frivolity and debauchery, to demean its people — ﴿That is because they are a people who do not reason﴾ — what they would have gained by answering it, had they answered it, and what they would bear for their mockery of it.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 59:

﴿Say, "O People of the Scripture, do you resent us only because we believe in Allah and in what has been revealed to us and what was revealed before, and because most of you are defiant?"﴾ The verse (i.e., do you deny and hate?)

[A group of Jews came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and asked him about which of the messengers he believed in. He said: "We believe in Allah and in what has been revealed to us, and what was revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob and the tribes, and what was given to Moses and Jesus and the prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and to Him we are submitting."] When he mentioned Jesus, they denied his prophethood and said: "We know of no religion more evil than yours." So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Do you resent?﴾ That is: do you hate and deny us, except our faith and your defiance? That is: you only hated our faith while you know that we are upon the truth, because you have defied by persisting in your religion out of love for leadership and your gaining of wealth through it. The estimation of His words ﴿and that most of you are defiant﴾ is: "and because most of you" with the waw being extra, and the meaning: because of your defiance you resented our faith.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 60:

His words: ﴿Say: Shall I inform you﴾ (aknabbi'ukum), i.e., shall I tell you. This is an answer to the statement of the Jews: "We do not know a people of a religion worse than you." So God said: ﴿Shall I inform you of something worse than that﴾, i.e., than what you say about them, namely the Muslims whom you reproached, ﴿as recompense (mathubah) with God? Those whom God has cursed﴾, meaning: it is those whom God has cursed, i.e., removed far from His mercy, ﴿and upon whom He has been angry, and made of them apes and swine﴾, meaning: the People of the Sabbath. ﴿And served the Taghut﴾ is a conjunction (ma'tuf) upon ﴿whom God has cursed﴾. "Served the Taghut" means obeyed Satan in what he embellished for them. ﴿Those are worse in place﴾, because their place is Saqar (Hell). ﴿And further astray from the right way﴾, i.e., the straight path, which is the religion of the Hanifiyyah (pure monotheism).

When this verse was revealed, the Muslims reproached the Jews and said: "O brothers of the apes and swine!" So they fell silent and were disgraced.

Al-Wahidi, al-Wajiz, on Surah 5, verse 61:

﴿And when they come to you, they say, "We believe,"﴾ meaning: the hypocrites among the Jews. ﴿while they had entered with disbelief, and they had gone out with it.﴾ That is: they entered and went out as disbelievers, and disbelief was with them in both their states.

**Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 62:**

﴿And you see many of them hastening toward sin and aggression﴾. They become bold in error and wrongdoing and rush toward it. ﴿And their consuming of what is unlawful (al-suht)﴾: that which they used to take as bribes (al-rasha) in exchange for concealing the truth. Then He censured their deed by saying: ﴿Wretched is what they used to do﴾.

﴿Why do the rabbis﴾ — that is, why do they not forbid them: "Lawlā" means "hal-lā" (why not) — ﴿their forbidding them﴾ from the ugliness of their deeds, ﴿the rabbis (al-rabbāniyyūn) and the scholars (al-aḥbār)﴾ — their learned men and their jurists — ﴿how evil is what they used to do﴾ when they left off rebuking them.

Note on the translation above: I have rendered the opening clause as a full English sentence for readability, but the source's wording is "Lawlā" (ﷺ-free) with the gloss "hallā" (why not), and I should be precise here: the faithful rendering is as follows.

**Translation:**

﴿Lawlā﴾ — that is, "hal-lā" (why not) — ﴿would that they forbade them﴾ from the ugliness of their deeds; ﴿the rabbis (al-rabbāniyyūn) and the scholars (al-aḥbār)﴾ — their learned men and their jurists; ﴿how evil is what they used to do﴾ when they left off rebuking them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 64:

﴿And the Jews say: "The hand of Allah is chained."﴾ Withheld from giving and from bestowing favours upon us. They said this when Allah, exalted is He, restrained from them, because of their disbelief in Muhammad (peace be upon him), the abundance and blessing that He had been bestowing upon them. So they said - may Allah curse them - by way of describing Him with stinginess: ﴿The hand of Allah is chained.﴾ His saying ﴿Their hands are chained﴾ means: they were made stingy and were burdened with stinginess, so they are the most miserly of people. ﴿And they are cursed for what they have said.﴾ They were punished in this world with the jizyah (poll tax), with humiliation, subjugation, famine and exile, and in the Hereafter with the Fire. ﴿Rather, both His hands are outspread.﴾ It was said: its meaning is a description with hyperbole of generosity and bounty. It was also said: its meaning is that His blessings are spread out, and the dual form indicates abundance, like the saying of the Arabs: (labbayka wa sa'dayka) ("at Your service, again and again"). It was also said: its meaning is: the blessing of this world and the blessing of the Hereafter. ﴿Both outspread; He spends however He wills.﴾ He provides as He wishes: if He wills, He restricts, and if He wills, He expands. ﴿And indeed, much of them will increase in transgression and disbelief through what has been revealed to you from your Lord.﴾ Whenever something of the Qur'an is revealed to you, they disbelieve in it, so their disbelief increases. ﴿And We have cast among them enmity and hatred﴾ among the groups of the Jews, and Allah made them divided and mutually hostile, as He said: ﴿You think them united, but their hearts are divided.﴾ ﴿Every time they kindle a fire for war, Allah extinguishes it.﴾ Every time they intend to fight you, Allah repels them and imposes fear upon them. ﴿And they strive throughout the land to cause corruption.﴾ That is: they strive to repel Islam and to erase the mention of the Prophet (ﷺ) from their books.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 65:

﴿And if the People of the Book had believed﴾ in Muhammad (ﷺ) ﴿and been mindful of God﴾ by abandoning Judaism and Christianity, ﴿We would have removed from them their misdeeds﴾, all that they had done before it reached them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 66:

﴿And if they had upheld the Torah and the Gospel﴾ — that is, acted upon what is in them of confirming you (ﷺ) — ﴿and what was revealed to them﴾ from the books of their prophets — ﴿they would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet﴾ — meaning, I would have sent down rain upon them and brought forth for them the produce of the earth whenever they wished. ﴿Among them is a moderate community﴾ — believers.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 67:

﴿O Messenger, deliver what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾. That is: do not be concerned about anyone, and do not leave out anything of what has been revealed to you out of fear that some harm will befall you. Deliver all of it openly. ﴿And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message﴾. If you conceal a single verse of what I have revealed to you, you have not conveyed My message. That is to say: whoever leaves out the delivery of part of it is like one who has not delivered it at all. ﴿And Allah will protect you from the people﴾, so that they do not reach you with harm. The exegetes said: The Prophet ﷺ was concerned for himself about the harm of the Jews and the disbelievers, and he would not openly denounce their religion or revile their gods. So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿O Messenger, deliver what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾. He said: "O Lord, how shall I act when I am one man and I fear that they will gang up against me?" So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message. And Allah will protect you from the people. Indeed, Allah does not guide the disbelieving people﴾, meaning: He does not guide the one who denies you.

﴿Say, O People of the Scripture, you are not upon anything﴾ of religion ﴿until you establish﴾ until you act upon what is in the two Scriptures of belief in Muhammad (ﷺ) and the description of his attributes. The rest of the verse has already been explained up to His words, ﴿So do not grieve over the disbelieving people.﴾ He says: Do not grieve over the People of the Scripture if they deny you.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 69:

﴿Indeed, those who believed and those who were Jews﴾ Its explanation has already preceded in Surat al-Baqarah.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 71:

﴿And they thought there would be no trial﴾ They supposed and reckoned that no punishment or torment would befall them for persisting in disbelief, by killing the prophets and denying the messengers. ﴿So they became blind and deaf﴾ to guidance, so they did not understand it. ﴿Then Allah turned toward them in forgiveness﴾ by sending Muhammad (ﷺ) as a caller to the straight path. ﴿Then many of them became blind and deaf again﴾ after the truth had become clear to them through Muhammad (peace be upon him). ﴿And Allah is All-Seeing of what they do﴾ of killing the prophets and denying the messengers.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 73:

﴿Indeed, those who said, "Indeed Allah is the third of three," have certainly disbelieved.﴾ That is: the third of three gods. The meaning is that they said: Allah is one of three gods: He, the Messiah, and Mary. They claimed that divinity is shared among these three, and thereby they disbelieved.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 74:

﴿The Messiah, son of Mary, is only a messenger; messengers had passed away before him.﴾ Meaning: he is a messenger, not a god, just as those before him were messengers. ﴿And his mother was a true believer (siddiqah)﴾ who affirmed the words of her Lord and His scriptures. ﴿They both used to eat food.﴾ He means: they are flesh and blood; they eat, drink, urinate and defecate, and these are not attributes of divinity. ﴿Look how We make the signs clear to them﴾ that is, We explain to them the matter of My lordship. ﴿Then look how they are turned away﴾ that is, they are diverted from the truth to which reflection on the signs leads.

Say (to the Christians): ﴿Do you worship besides Allah that which possesses neither harm nor benefit for you?﴾ He means: the Messiah, because none possesses that except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. ﴿And Allah is the All-Hearing﴾ of your disbelief, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾ of what your hearts conceal.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 77:

﴿Say, "O People of the Scripture, do not exceed the bounds in your religion beyond the truth"﴾, meaning: the Jews and the Christians. ﴿And do not follow the desires of a people who had gone astray before and led many astray and strayed from the sound way.﴾ Meaning: their leaders who passed away from both groups. That is, do not follow your predecessors in what they innovated by their own desires. ﴿Do not exceed the bounds in your religion beyond the truth﴾ means: do not go beyond the limit concerning Jesus. The exaggeration of the Jews regarding him is in denying him and attributing him to illegitimacy, and the exaggeration of the Christians regarding him is their claim of his divinity. As for His saying ﴿beyond the truth﴾, it means: opposing the truth. ﴿And do not follow the desires of a people who had gone astray before﴾, meaning: their leaders who passed away from both groups, that is, do not follow your predecessors in what they innovated by their own desires. ﴿And [they] strayed from the sound way﴾, meaning: they strayed from the right path by their leading many astray.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 78:

﴿Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed﴾ meaning: the People of the Sabbath and the People of the Table, ﴿upon the tongue of Dawud﴾ (David) (peace be upon him), because when they transgressed, Dawud, peace be upon him, said: "O Allah, curse them and make them a sign for Your creation," so they were transformed into apes. ﴿And Isa ibn Maryam﴾ (Jesus, son of Mary) (peace be upon him), because he cursed those among the People of the Table who did not believe, and said: "O Allah, curse them as You cursed the People of the Sabbath," so they were transformed into swine.

﴿They did not forbid one another from wrongdoing that they committed.﴾

Note on the Arabic: the verb "لا يتناهون" (lā yatanāhawn) means "they do not stop themselves / do not refrain," and al-Wahidi glosses it with "لا ينتهون" (lā yantahūn), "they do not desist," so the phrase is explained as they did not desist from a wrongful act that they had done.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 80:

﴿You see many of them﴾ — of the Jews — ﴿allying themselves with those who disbelieve﴾ — the disbelievers of Makkah. ﴿Evil is what their souls have sent forth for them, [for] that Allah has become angry with them﴾ — evil is what they sent forth as deeds for their return in the Hereafter: the anger of Allah upon them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 82:

﴿You will surely find﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿the most intense of the people in enmity toward those who believe to be the Jews﴾. That is because they backed the polytheists against the believers, out of envy toward the Prophet (ﷺ). ﴿And you will surely find the nearest of them in affection toward those who believe to be those who say, "We are Christians"﴾. It means: al-Najashi (the Negus) and his delegation, who came from Abyssinia to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), believed in him, and it does not refer to all Christians. ﴿That﴾, meaning: the nearness of affection, ﴿is because among them are priests (qissisin) and monks (ruhban)﴾, that is: scholars who know the charge of Jesus to believe in Muhammad (peace be upon him). ﴿And that they are not arrogant﴾ in following the truth, as the Jews and the idol-worshippers are arrogant.

And when they hear what has been sent down to the Messenger: this refers to the Najashi (the Negus) and his companions. Ja'far ibn Abi Talib recited to them in Abyssinian (بالحبشة) (كهعيص) (the disjointed letters that open Surah Maryam), and they did not stop weeping. This is His saying: ﴿You see their eyes overflowing with tears because of the truth they have recognised﴾, meaning what was sent down to Muhammad (ﷺ), and it is the truth. ﴿They say: Our Lord, we have believed﴾ and affirmed, ﴿so write us down among the witnesses﴾, among the community of Muhammad (ﷺ) who bear witness to the truth.

﴿And why should we not believe in God﴾, that is: what would be for us if we abandoned belief in God? ﴿and what has come to us of the truth﴾, that is: the Qur'an? ﴿And﴾ we ﴿hope that our Lord will admit us﴾ into Paradise ﴿along with the people of Muhammad (peace be upon him)﴾. They mean: they have nothing if they do not believe in the Qur'an, and their hope of entering Paradise will not be realized.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 85:

﴿So Allah rewarded them for what they said.﴾ That is: for what they asked of Allah by their saying: ﴿"So record us among the witnesses."﴾ And by their saying: ﴿"And we hope that our Lord will admit us [into the company of] the righteous people."﴾ The verse continues: ﴿Gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide eternally. And that is the reward of the doers of good.﴾ That is: the reward, ﴿the reward of the doers of good﴾, meaning the monotheists (al-muwahhidun). Then he mentioned the threat for those among the People of the Book and others who disbelieved, saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 87:

﴿O you who have believed, do not prohibit the good things which Allah has made lawful for you﴾ Some people among the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) resolved and pledged among themselves that they would forbid themselves good food, that they would fast by day and stand in prayer by night, and that they would castrate themselves (yakhsa'u anfusahum). So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse, and He named castration "transgression" (i'tida'). When this verse was revealed, they said: "O Messenger of Allah, we had sworn an oath to that effect," so it was revealed:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 89:

﴿Allah will not hold you accountable for the unintentional oaths in your oaths﴾. We have explained this in Surah al-Baqarah. ﴿But He will hold you accountable for the oaths you have sworn in earnest﴾, which is when a person intends a matter, swears by Allah, and binds himself to the oath in his heart deliberately. ﴿Its expiation﴾, if you break them, ﴿is feeding ten needy persons﴾, giving each needy person a mudd, which is one and a third ratl, and this is His saying: ﴿from the average of what you feed your families﴾, because this quantity is average in terms of satisfying hunger. It was also said: ﴿from the best of what you feed your families﴾, such as wheat and dates. ﴿Or clothing them﴾, which is the least that falls under the name of clothing: a garment (izar), a cloak (rida'), and a shirt (qamis). ﴿Or freeing a slave﴾, meaning a believing one. The one who makes expiation for an oath has the choice among these three. ﴿But whoever does not find [the means]﴾, meaning he does not have surplus from his own sustenance and that of his dependents for the day and night sufficient to feed ten needy persons, ﴿then﴾ he must fast ﴿for three days﴾. ﴿And guard your oaths﴾, so do not swear oaths, and guard them against breaking.

O you who have believed, indeed intoxicants (khamr), gambling (maysir), idols (ansab), and divining arrows (azlam) are a defilement of Satan's handiwork, so avoid it.

Here the commentary (al-Wahidi, al-Wajiz) explains each term:

"Khamr" means the drinks that are fermented until they become strong and intoxicating.

"Maysir" means gambling in all its forms.

"Ansab" means idols.

"Azlam" means the divining arrows (qidah al-istiqsam) mentioned at the beginning of the surah.

"Rijs" means filthy and ugly.

"Min 'amal al-shaytan" means of what Satan adorns for the children of Adam.

"Fajtanibuhu" means keep away from it, be apart from it.

Al-Wahidi, al-Wajiz, on surah 5, verse 91:

﴿Indeed, Satan only wants to cause enmity and hatred to arise among you through intoxicants and gambling﴾ That is because of the enmity, the ugly conduct, and the daring to do what the intellect forbids that take place among their practitioners. ﴿And to prevent you from the remembrance of Allah and from the prayer﴾ Because whoever occupies himself with them is kept from the remembrance of Allah and from the prayer. ﴿So will you not desist?﴾ (a question that carries the meaning of a command). They said: "We have desisted." Then He commanded obedience, saying:

**Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 92:**

﴿And obey Allah and obey the Messenger, and beware [of what is forbidden]﴾: the prohibited things and the forbidden acts. ﴿But if you turn away﴾ from obedience, ﴿then know that upon Our Messenger is only the clear delivery﴾. So he has no duty except to deliver [the message]. If you obey, [well and good]; otherwise you deserve punishment. When the prohibition of wine was revealed, they said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you say about our brothers who died while they were drinking it and eating gambling [winnings]?" So [Allah] revealed:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 93:

﴿There is no blame upon those who have believed and done righteous deeds for what they ate﴾ of wine and gambling before their prohibition, ﴿when they fear Allah﴾ from sins and polytheism, ﴿and then fear Allah﴾ they persevered in their piety, ﴿and then fear Allah﴾ from wronging the servants, along with adding goodness to it.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 94:

﴿O you who have believed, Allah will surely test you with something of the game (ṣayd) that your hands and your lances can reach﴾. This was in the year of al-Ḥudaybiyah. Wild animals and birds were coming to them in their camp in great numbers while they were in the state of iḥrām ( iḥrām: the sacred state of pilgrimage in which certain acts are forbidden). It was a trial from Allah, the Exalted. ﴿That your hands can reach﴾ means: the young birds and the small ones. ﴿And your lances﴾ means: the large ones. ﴿That Allah may make evident﴾ means: that Allah may see. ﴿Who fears Him unseen﴾ means: who fears Allah though he has not seen Him. ﴿And whoever transgresses after that﴾ means: wrongs by taking the game ﴿after this﴾, after the prohibition. ﴿For him is a painful punishment﴾.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 95:

﴿O you who have believed, do not kill game while you are in the state of ihram﴾. God forbade game to the muhrim (one in the state of ihram, the consecrated state for pilgrimage). He may not approach game in any way for as long as he remains in ihram.

﴿And whoever among you kills it intentionally, then there is a penalty equivalent to what he killed from among the livestock﴾. That is: he must pay a penalty equivalent to the slain animal in its form. So for an ostrich there is a badanah (a camel or cow sacrificed as an offering), for a wild ass a cow, and for a hyena a ram, according to this estimate.

﴿Judged by two just men﴾ means two upright men will judge concerning the game, ﴿among you﴾, that is, from among the people of your religion. They will look at what is most similar to it among the livestock and rule accordingly.

﴿As an offering reaching the Kaaba﴾ means: the like of that.

﴿Or expiation by fasting﴾. When the muhrim kills game, he has a choice. If he wishes, he may compensate with an animal of livestock similar to it. If he wishes, he may value the equivalent in dirhams, then use the dirhams to buy food, then give it in charity. If he wishes, he may fast a day for each mudd (a unit of dry measure).

﴿That he may taste the consequence of his affair﴾, that is, the penalty for what he did.

﴿God has pardoned what has passed﴾, that is, before the prohibition.

﴿And whoever returns, God will take retribution from him﴾. Whoever returns to killing game while in ihram is judged a second time, and he is under threat of punishment.

﴿And God is Mighty﴾, invincible, ﴿Owner of retribution﴾ against the people of His disobedience.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 96:

﴿Lawful for you is the game of the sea﴾ (ṣayd al-baḥr), that which is caught from within it. This permission is general for everyone, whether in the state of ihram (muḥrim) or not (muḥill). ﴿And its food﴾, which is what the water has receded from and which was not hunted. ﴿As a provision for you and for the travelers﴾, a benefit for the resident and the traveler, who sell it and take it as provision. Then he repeated the prohibition of hunting in the state of ihram, saying: ﴿And the game of the land is forbidden to you as long as you are in the state of ihram. And fear Allah, to whom you will be gathered﴾, fear Allah, to whom you will be resurrected.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 97:

﴿Allah made the Ka'bah, the Sacred House,﴾ meaning: the House which He made sacred, such that game may not be hunted near it, and such that its vegetation may not be cut, for the Hajj and the performance of the rites. ﴿And the sacred month﴾ meaning: the sacred months, and so it is mentioned in the singular, as a collective noun. ﴿And the offerings and the garlands﴾ We have mentioned them at the beginning of the surah. This phrase was mentioned after the mention of the House because they are among the means of the Hajj, so they were mentioned along with it. ﴿That﴾ meaning: that which I have informed you of in this surah, of the reports of the prophets, the conditions of the hypocrites and the Jews, and other matters. ﴿So that you may know that Allah knows whatever is in the heavens...﴾ the verse. Meaning: this shows you that nothing is hidden from Him.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 100:

﴿Say, "The evil and the good are not equal, even if the abundance of evil impresses you."﴾ That is: the unlawful (ḥarām) and the lawful (ḥalāl). And this refers to the people of this world, who are impressed by the abundance of wealth and the adornment of worldly life.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 101:

﴿O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would distress you﴾ It was revealed when the Prophet was asked so persistently that they pressed him with questions. He stood up in anger, delivered a sermon, and said: "Do not ask me about anything during this standing of mine except that I will inform you of it." A man from the Banu Sahm, who was disparaging his lineage, stood up and said: "Who is my father?" He said: "Your father is Hudhafah." Another stood up and said: "Where am I?" He said: "In the Fire." So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse and forbade them to ask him about what his answer would distress them, such as the question of one who asked about his place and was told: "In the Fire." ﴿And if you ask about them﴾ i.e., about things ﴿when the Qur'an is being revealed﴾ concerning them ﴿they will be disclosed to you﴾, meaning: what the Qur'an reveals concerning an obligation, a prohibition, or a ruling, and there is a need to clarify it. So if you ask about them at that time, they will be made clear to you. ﴿Allah has pardoned you concerning them﴾, i.e., concerning your questioning, which the Prophet ﷺ disliked, and for which there was no need on your part to have it clarified. He forbade them to return to the like of that and informed them that He had pardoned what they had done. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing﴾, who does not hasten to punishment. Then He informed them about the state of one who burdens himself with asking about what he was not obligated to, and He said:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 102:

﴿Qad saalaha﴾ (Indeed, they asked for them): that is, the signs. ﴿Qawmun min qablikum﴾ (a people before you), and the rest of the verse: meaning the people of Jesus, who asked for the table spread (al-Ma'idah) and then disbelieved in it, and the people of Salih, who asked for the she-camel and then hamstrung her.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 103:

﴿Allah did not ordain any bahirah﴾ That is: He did not prescribe it, nor command it. The bahirah (a she-camel that had given birth to five offspring, the last of which was male): they would slit its ear, refrain from riding it, and from slaughtering it. ﴿Nor sa'ibah﴾ This is what they would release (sayyibuhu) for their idols, by a vow binding upon them: if a sick person recovered, or a need of theirs was fulfilled. ﴿Nor wasilah﴾ A ewe, if she gave birth to a female, it was theirs; if she gave birth to a male, they dedicated it to their idols; and if she gave birth to a male and a female, they said: she has joined (wasalat) her brother, so they did not slaughter the male for their idols. ﴿Nor ham﴾ When a stallion had sired ten offspring, they said: its back has been protected (qad hama zahruhu), so it was not ridden, nor was it benefited from, and it was released for their idols, so no load was put upon it. ﴿But those who disbelieve invent lies against Allah﴾ They fabricate falsehoods about Allah concerning the prohibition of these livestock, and they themselves made them forbidden, not Allah. ﴿And most of them﴾ meaning: the followers of their leaders, who established for them the prohibition of these livestock. ﴿do not reason﴾ that this is a lie and a fabrication against Allah by the leaders.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 104:

﴿And when it is said to them, "Come to what Allah has sent down"﴾ in the Qur'an, concerning the permitting of what you have forbidden, ﴿they say, "Sufficient for us is what we found our fathers upon"﴾ of religion, ﴿even though their fathers knew nothing and were not guided?﴾ explained in Surat al-Baqarah.

O you who have believed, take care of yourselves; the one who has gone astray cannot harm you once you are guided. To Allah is your return, all of you, and He will inform you of what you used to do.

Al-Wahidi, al-Wajiz:

﴿O you who have believed, take care of yourselves﴾ guard them from involvement in sins and persistence in wrongdoing. ﴿The one who has gone astray cannot harm you﴾ from among the People of the Book ﴿once you are guided﴾ you yourselves ﴿To Allah is your return, all of you﴾ your final destination and the destination of those who opposed you. ﴿And He will inform you of what you used to do﴾ He will recompense you for your deeds.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 106:

﴿O you who have believed, let there be [a witness] between you, when death approaches one of you at the time of bequest, two just men among you as witnesses or two others from outside your community if you are travelling throughout the land and the disaster of death strikes you.﴾ This verse was revealed concerning the story of Tamim, ʿAdi and Budayl, who went out as merchants to al-Sham. Budayl fell ill, and he handed over his goods to the two of them and bequeathed to them that they should deliver them to his family when they returned. They took from his goods a vessel of silver and returned the rest to his family. The family learned of their treachery and brought the matter to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Allah the Exalted revealed these verses. The meaning of the verse: "Let there be a witness for you" when death approaches one of you and you wish to make a bequest, "two just men among you" from among the people of your religion, whom you call as witnesses to the bequest, "or two others from outside your community," from outside your religion, if you are "travelling" (ḍarabtum), i.e. journeying, "throughout the land and the disaster of death strikes you." Allah knew that some people travel and are accompanied on their journey by People of the Book and not by Muslims, and death comes upon them and they find no Muslim to witness their bequest. So He said: "or two others from outside your community." Thus the two dhimmis are accepted as witnesses on a journey only (specifically), when no one else is available (their testimony is accepted in that matter).

And His saying: ﴿You detain them after the prayer, and they swear by Allah, if you doubt, "We will not sell it for any price, even if it were [to] a near relative, and we will not conceal the testimony of Allah; indeed, we would then be among the sinful."﴾ That is: if you doubt their testimony and suspect that they have betrayed, you detain them for the oath after the afternoon prayer, and they swear by Allah and say in their oath: "We do not sell Allah for any worldly gain, nor do we favour anyone in our testimony," "even if he were a near relative," even if the one testified for were a near relative, "and we will not conceal the testimony of Allah," i.e. the testimony which Allah commanded to be upheld, "indeed, we would then be among the sinful" if we concealed it.

When they were brought to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered that they be made to swear. That was because they were Christians, while Budayl was a Muslim. They swore that they had taken nothing beyond what they had handed to the heirs and had concealed nothing, and their way was let go. Then the vessel was found in their possession, and they said: "We bought it from him." So the matter was brought before the Prophet (ﷺ), and there was revealed his saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 107:

﴿Then if it becomes known﴾, i.e., it becomes apparent and is discovered, ﴿that the two deserved sin﴾, i.e., they became liable for it through betrayal and breaking the oath, ﴿then two others shall stand in their place﴾ from among the heirs, namely those ﴿against whom the claim is made﴾, i.e., against whom the bequest or the appointment as executors is claimed, for the bequest is claimed from the heirs, ﴿the nearest of kin﴾ to the deceased, i.e., the closest relatives to him. The meaning is: two men from the relatives of the deceased stand in the place of the two of them in the oath, and they swear by God: "We have discovered the treachery and the lying and the substitution of the two dhimmis," and this is His saying: ﴿They shall swear by God: "Our testimony is more worthy than their testimony,"﴾ i.e., our oath is more worthy than their oath, ﴿and we have not transgressed,﴾ in what we have said. When this verse was revealed, two of the heirs of the deceased stood up and swore by God that the two had betrayed and lied, and the vessel was handed over to the heirs of the deceased.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 108:

﴿That﴾ i.e., what He has ruled in this matter and made clear, namely the return of the oath, is ﴿closer﴾ to bringing the testimony as it was, ﴿or they fear﴾ i.e., closer to their fearing ﴿that oaths will be returned﴾ upon the heirs of the deceased after the oaths of the executors, so that they swear to their betrayal and lying and are exposed. ﴿And fear Allah﴾ lest you swear false oaths or betray a trust. ﴿And listen﴾ to the admonition. ﴿And Allah does not guide the defiant people﴾ He does not guide to righteousness those who persist in their disobedience.

"On the Day when Allah will gather the Messengers, and He will say: ﴿What was the response you received?﴾" That is: remember that day. ﴿Then He will say﴾ to them: ﴿What response did you receive?﴾ What did your peoples answer you regarding monotheism (tawhid)? ﴿They will say, "We have no knowledge"﴾ because of the terror of that Day; they will be dumbfounded and forget the answer, then they will answer after their minds have returned to them, and they will testify for those who believed them and against those who denied them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 110:

﴿When God said, "O Jesus, son of Mary"﴾. The explanation (tafsir) of the verse has passed up to His saying: ﴿and when I restrained the Children of Israel from you﴾, i.e., from killing you.

"And when I inspired the disciples" — that is, I caused them to know (or: inspired them).

Note on the rendering: the Arabic "أوحيت" here is glossed by al-Wahidi as "ألهمتهم" (I put into their hearts / inspired them).

The Disciples said, "O Jesus, son of Mary, can your Lord send down to us a table from heaven?" (Qur'an 5:112, in part: "When the disciples said, 'O Jesus, son of Mary, can your Lord send down to us a table spread from heaven?'")

Note on the text: the commentary quotes the verse as ﴿إِذْ قَالَ الْحَوَارِيُّونَ يَا عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ هل يستطيع ربك﴾, and the translation above has been rendered as a single translation of the quoted words.

Correction to the above: the translation should follow the passage exactly. Here it is:

When the Disciples said: "O Jesus, son of Mary, can your Lord send down to us a table from heaven?" They did not doubt His power, but its meaning was: Would your Lord accept your supplication, and would it be easy for Him to send down to us a table from the heaven as a sign (ʿalam) for you and a proof of your truthfulness? Jesus said: "Fear God" — that you should ask Him for something that the nations before you did not ask for.

He said: "We want to eat from it" — meaning: we want to ask for this for its own sake — "and our hearts may be set at rest" — we increase in certainty of your truthfulness — "and that we may be among its witnesses" — witnesses to God with regard to His oneness, and to you with regard to prophethood. And His saying

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 114:

﴿Be for us a festival (ʿīd) for the first of us and the last of us﴾, that is: we shall take the day on which it descends as a festival, which we and those who come after us will honor. ﴿And a sign from You﴾, a proof of Your oneness and of the truth of Your Prophet. ﴿And provide for us﴾ [a meal] through it, food that we may eat.

And His saying: ﴿Whoever among you disbelieves after that﴾, i.e., after the sending down of the Table (al-Ma'idah), ﴿then I will punish him with a punishment with which I will not punish anyone among the worlds﴾. He meant: a kind of punishment with which none of the people of their time, other than them, will be punished.

"And when Allah says, "O Jesus, son of Mary," (واذكر يا مُحمَّدُ حين يقول الله تعالى يوم القيامة) — "Remember, O Muhammad, when Allah the Exalted says on the Day of Resurrection:" ﴿Did you say to the people, "Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah?"﴾ This is an interrogative whose meaning is reproach, directed at those who claimed this about the Messiah, so that the Messiah may deny it to them and the proof will be established against them. ﴿He will say, "Glory be to You"﴾ — that is, Your exoneration from every evil. ﴿You know what is in my soul﴾ — that is, what is in my secret and what I conceal. ﴿And I do not know what is in Yourself﴾ — that is, what You conceal and what is known only to You, which You have not disclosed to us.

And His saying: ﴿And I was a witness over them﴾, meaning: I was witnessing what they did while I was still living among them. ﴿So when You caused me to die﴾, meaning: You raised me up to the heaven. ﴿You were the Watcher over them﴾, the Guardian over them. ﴿And You are Witness over all things﴾, meaning: You witnessed my statement concerning them, and after You raised me up, You witnessed what they say after me.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 5, verse 118:

﴿If You punish them﴾, meaning: those who disbelieved in You, ﴿indeed they are Your servants﴾, and You are just concerning them. ﴿And if You forgive them﴾, meaning: those among them who repent and believe, ﴿indeed You are the Almighty, none can prevent You from what You will, the All-Wise in that.﴾

God said: "This is a day" — meaning: the Day of Resurrection — "on which the truthful will benefit from their truthfulness" in the world, "because it is the day of reward and recompense. "Allah is pleased with them" for their obedience, "and they are pleased with Him" for His reward. "That is the great triumph," because they have triumphed by attaining Paradise.
﴿To God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth.﴾ He exalted Himself above what the Christians said: that there is a god with Him.
